items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: when I did “Yardbird Suite” that was a few years ago with Anthony... We did it in an album called “One Night in Vienna.”

ctx.x: I saw another interesting quote from you describing the content of The Primacy of the Ear. I’m not sure you wrote this, but the person who wrote the review said one thing that you addressed was how to listen to your musical heroes without being consumed by them. And it made me think of Charlie Parker and everybody who came after him. So how do you not become consumed by your musical heroes?

Well first, speaking for myself, I don’t know if I am or not. I know that a colleague of mine who runs the Third Stream Contemporary Improvisation Department, I’ve studied Yiddish music with him, Klezmer, and he said, “By all means bring in your dark clouds and your sensibility but try to occasionally at the beginning get to the style and let’s hear more melody.” And I’ve tried to do that, sometimes succeeded, often not. I don’t think I wrote that but I think probably somebody quoted it. And who will decide…
